<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Two defects, one pipeline, measured in prod on 2026-08-30 under conversation-ingest load. (1) TRUNCATION: the 2026-08-27 ruling ('truncate now, split later') embeds only a prefix of any input over the model's per-input cap (8192 tokens); conversation turns (20KB+ tool dumps) hit this constantly, so each such turn's TAIL is semantically unsearchable. 'Later' is now: split oversize inputs into overlapping chunks, each with its own vector, grandfathering every existing vector as chunk 0. (2) POISON BATCHES: empty-bodied turns (raw_hash e3b0c442... — the empty-string sha) become embed jobs whose empty text reaches Azure and rejects the WHOLE merged call — measured: one empty turn rejected 530 innocent texts; three poison turns cost 9 rejected calls / 1,639 texts collateral in one wave, and the failed rows revive at every boot sweep (we now bounce on every merge). Filter at mint AND at batch assembly. Prior art both sides: fs2's content-type-aware chunker (ChunkItem(node_id, chunk_index, text), code=400/docs=800/smart=8000 token targets, line-span tracking) and fs3's own dedupe-by-element ranking which ALREADY collapses multiple vectors (raw+smart) per element — chunks widen 2 to N with no ranking redesign.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- Every byte of an oversize input is semantically searchable: N overlapping chunk vectors per (source_hash, kind), not a truncated prefix.
- No empty or whitespace-only input ever reaches a provider: filtered at job mint (turn/element enrichment enqueue) AND asserted at batch assembly (defense in depth).
- Existing vectors are grandfathered as chunk_no=0 — zero re-embedding, zero backfill cost on migration.
- Existing poison rows are healed: empty-input embed jobs are terminally retired (not boot-sweep-revived), with a receipt of how many.
- Search behaviour is unchanged for single-chunk content and strictly better for chunked content (the tail can now match); ranking still returns ONE row per element via the existing dedupe.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No change to the 8192-token per-input cap itself or to provider adapters' wire shapes.
- No content-type-aware chunk SIZING in v1 (fs2's code=400/docs=800 refinement is a named future; v1 uses one near-cap window size + overlap for all kinds).
- No re-embedding of existing truncated rows (the truncated=true inventory is a cheap later backfill, explicitly deferred).
- No summarize-lane changes; no ranking algorithm changes beyond consuming N chunk rows through the existing element dedupe.
- No queue/lane redesign — this rides the existing embed lane, batch planner, and token-budget splitting untouched.
